hypothesis: The type inference algorithm for constructor calls is missing the logic to propagate property requirements backwards from the constructor's formal parameters to the actual arguments, specifically when the argument is an anonymous object literal.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the TypeInference class to correctly handle the traversal of constructor arguments and ensure that property requirements are correctly inferred and applied to the argument object.
experiment_rationale: The failing test case explicitly demonstrates that the compiler fails to infer the expected object structure when a constructor is invoked. Since the fix is in TypeInference, it confirms the logic for inferring types during constructor calls is flawed.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the type inference logic (a computational procedure) to correctly propagate type information during constructor calls. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability omission (Function/Class/Object). It is a procedural error in how the compiler processes type inference for specific language constructs.
evidence_gaps: The exact lines of code in TypeInference were not provided, but the class name and test failure are sufficient to identify the algorithmic nature of the fix.
